articles.title: SHIP INTERNAL TOOLS WITHOUT PULLING ENGINEERS OFF YOUR ROADMAP.
articles.summary: Someone on your ops team just built a renewals tracker in Cursor. Now they want to point it at real company data, and you're about to get a Slack message. WorkOS Atlas [5] hosts these apps privately behind company SSO. Admins control who can open each app and which internal tools it can connect to, so builders use approved connections without ever touching an API key. The team gets their tracker. You stay on the roadmap.

YOUR AI AGENT REMEMBERS EVERYTHING. THAT'S THE PROBLEM
articles.summary: Persistent memory can feed stale facts back to an agent after circumstances change. This piece covers background passes that review and rewrite stored memories and asks how systems should handle corrections, forgetting, and portability.

articles.title: SWIFTUI DOESN'T HAVE A LIST. IT WRAPS SOMEONE ELSE'S
articles.summary: Runtime inspection found that SwiftUI's List wraps NSOutlineView on macOS and UICollectionView on iPhone and iPad. SwiftUI still computes its own diffs and hosts each row in a SwiftUI view, so using the same underlying container leaves room for different update costs.

articles.title: STREAMING LLM RESPONSES WITHOUT RENDERING EVERY TOKEN
articles.summary: Give your streaming relay explicit completion and error events, and abort upstream generation when the client disconnects. Buffer incoming tokens and render at most once per animation frame so the browser can keep up.

articles.title: SUPERINTELLIGENCE IS ARRIVING
articles.summary: A reported AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis is a sign that superintelligence is approaching. The industry should build AI that expands human agency and keeps people in control.

articles.title: ASSUME PEOPLE ARE NOT INTERESTED IN YOUR BLOG POST
articles.summary: Open by telling readers who needs to pay attention so everyone else can move on. In Slack or Teams, put the essentials in the first three to five lines and leave the details in the thread.

Toptal AI acts as the single partner for all of their AI ambitions.

INTRODUCING INKLING 2 MINI
articles.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released an open-weight model that runs its middle layers three times per token and uses about 20 GB of memory. The lab reports a 48.2% score on DeepSWE v1.1, with evaluation setups varying across models.

articles.title: IT'S A PLAN
articles.summary: It's a Plan is a self-hosted issue tracker where teams can assign work to AI agents alongside human teammates. Agents have their own roles and permissions, and an assignment, mention, or schedule can start a run.

articles.title: BECOME A FOUNDING MEMBER OF TLDR'S AI COMMUNITY (2 MINUTE FORM)
articles.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join [16].

articles.title: PERPLEXITY AND INTELLIGENCE
articles.summary: OpenAI reports that log perplexity on its held-out dataset fell from about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 to 0.91 for GPT-4. It proposes using perplexity alongside other measures to set shared safety thresholds, while acknowledging that different evaluation datasets make cross-lab comparisons difficult.

articles.title: TEACHING A WEB PAGE TO READ A CHESS BOARD
articles.summary: This browser demo reconstructs a chess position from a screenshot in about a quarter of a second using a 131 KB model and plain JavaScript. Inference stays on the device. The system is designed for flat screenshots and diagrams.

articles.title: I ANALYZED THE AI STACK USED BY 40,000+ COMPANIES
articles.summary: An analysis of vendor disclosures found that 44.8% of companies naming an AI model provider listed at least two. Anthropic and OpenAI led the counts, while routers grew fastest over the month studied, driven mainly by OpenRouter.

articles.title: FOXIT: 10 PDF MCP SERVERS FOR AI AGENTS, COMPARED
articles.summary: Local servers, cloud APIs and self-hosted toolkits handle agent PDF work differently. See what each one reads, modifies and charges for.

A BEGINNER'S GUIDE TO LOCAL AI WITH INKLING, QWEN, AND UNSLOTH
articles.summary: Set up Unsloth Desktop on Windows, pick a quantized Inkling or Qwen model that leaves enough GPU memory for your context window, and share it over your home network.

articles.title: PATTERN ENGINEERING
articles.summary: Engineering teams can make coding agents more reliable by turning recurring workflows into reusable patterns and giving agents ways to verify their work.

articles.title: A SHORT HISTORY OF READ STREAMS IN POSTGRES
articles.summary: Postgres read streams combine adjacent disk pages into a single read, but a page already in shared buffers can split the range into two requests.

articles.title: WHAT WE LEARNED OPERATING AUTH FOR 1,000+ APIS
articles.summary: After a bug discarded newly rotated OAuth refresh tokens and forced users to reconnect, Nango began saving replacement tokens immediately and allowing only one refresh at a time per connection.
